headline_marked: Apple's iOS 27 [[overhauls Siri's voice]] with new expressiveness
headline: Apple's iOS 27 overhauls Siri's voice with new expressiveness
summary: New Siri Expressive Voice will offer more natural and customizable delivery, but requires the latest hardware for full features.
details: Apple is set to significantly enhance Siri's vocal capabilities with the upcoming iOS 27 update, introducing a more expressive and natural-sounding voice. This overhaul aims to bring Siri closer to the advanced AI assistant features offered by competitors.

For users with the latest hardware, including iPhone 17 Pro models and iPads with M4 chips or newer and 12GB of RAM, Siri's expressiveness and pace will be fully customizable. This allows for greater control over Siri's delivery, making interactions more nuanced.

While the full suite of expressive voice features is reserved for high-end devices, all iPhones from the SE second generation and iPhone 11 onwards will receive the iOS 27 update. However, the depth of Apple Intelligence features will vary across these devices.

Beyond the new expressiveness, iOS 27 also allows users to adjust Siri's speaking rate and pause time. These accessibility features, available in Settings > Accessibility > Siri, offer further control over Siri's response behavior, regardless of hardware limitations.

Users can also configure Siri's response style, choosing between spoken responses, quiet responses, or on-screen text only. Additional settings include options for listening for atypical speech and controlling interruptions, enhancing overall usability.

headline_marked: [[DLSS 5]] mod boosts FPS by 127% using a second GPU
headline: DLSS 5 mod boosts FPS by 127% using a second GPU
summary: A new mod allows DLSS 5 neural rendering to run on a separate GPU, significantly increasing frame rates in games like Cyberpunk 2077.
details: A developer has created an astonishing mod that utilizes a second GPU to handle Nvidia's DLSS 5 neural rendering, boosting frame rates by up to 127% in some cases. This technique separates the game's rendering from the post-processing, with the first GPU handling the visuals and a second GPU dedicated to the neural upscaling.

The mod, dubbed MGPU Bridge, works by reading each finished frame from the primary rendering GPU and sending it to a second GPU for DLSS 5 processing. The results are then displayed on a monitor connected to the second GPU, meaning the rendering GPU is completely free of the neural workload and runs cooler.

Demonstrations were shown using Cyberpunk 2077 and a cinematic video from The Blood of Dawnwalker. While not official benchmarks, the developer shared performance figures indicating significant gains. For example, in The Blood of Dawnwalker demo at 1080p, the dual-GPU setup with DLSS 5 on the second card retained 86% of the potential performance gain, compared to about a third when DLSS 5 ran on the same card.

This method is noted to be different from Nvidia's SLI technology, which split frame rendering between GPUs. Instead, it's compared to the dedicated PhysX cards of the past. The mod requires a dual-GPU setup and a second display, and it does double the display latency.

The project is available on GitHub for users to try themselves. While it offers impressive performance boosts and cooler temperatures on the rendering card (up to 21 degrees Celsius cooler in one test), it's important to remember this is a third-party mod and not Nvidia's intended implementation of DLSS 5.
